sections.shortTitle: N -W F P Ministers Code of Conduct Ordinance 1997
sections.description:
Short title extent and commencement

NORTH﷓WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE MIMSTERS (CODE OF CONDUCT)
ORDINANCE, 1997
NORTH‑WEST FRONTIER
PROVINCE MIMSTERS (CODE OF CONDUCT) ORDINANCE, 1997
An Ordinance to provide for the
Code of Conduct for Ministers of the North‑West Frontier Province
[Gazette of N.‑W.F.P.,
Extraordinary 27th January, 1997].
No Legis. 1(3)/97/581, dated 27‑1‑1997.‑‑‑The
following Ordinance by the Governor of the North‑West Frontier Province
is hereby published for general information:
Whereas it is expedient to
provide for the Code of Conduct for Ministers of the North‑West Frontier
Province in the manner hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the Provincial
Assembly is not in session and the Governor of the North‑West Frontier
Province is satisfied that the circumstances exist which render it necessary to
take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of
the powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 128 of the Constitution of the
Islamic Republic of Pakistan, the Governor of the North‑West Frontier
Province is pleased to make and promulgate the following Ordinance:‑‑
1. Short title and
commencement.‑‑(1) This Ordinance may be called the North‑West
Frontier Province Ministers (Code of Conduct) Ordinance, 1997.
(2) It shall come in to force at
once.
(3) It shall apply to all
Ministers of the North‑West Frontier Province.

2. Definitions.‑‑In
this Ordinance, unless the context to otherwise requires, the following
expressions shall have the meanings hereby respectively assigned to them,‑‑
(a) "Appendix" means
the Appendix to this Ordinance;
(b) "Chief Secretary"
means the Chief Secretary as defined in the Rules of Business;
(c) "Department" means
the Department as defined in the Rules of Business.
(d) "Government" means
the Government of the North‑West Frontier Province.
(e) "Minister" means
the Minister‑in‑Charge of the Department to which a particular case
pertains and includes;
(i) the Chief Minister; and
(ii) a Member of the Provincial

Parliamentary Secretary;
(f) "Ministry of Foreign
Affairs" means the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan;
(g) "Oath of office"
means the oath administered to a Minister under Article 132(2) of the
Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan;
(h) "Province" means
the Province of the North‑West Frontier
(i) "Provincial
Assembly" mead the Provincial Assembly of the Province;
(j) "Rules of Business"
means the North‑West Frontier Province Government Rules of Business,
1985;
(k) "Secretary" means
the Secretary as defined in the Rules of Business; and
(l) "Toshakhana" means
the store‑house maintained by Government for safe custody of movable
property vesting or deemed to be vesting in Government.

Whereas it is expedient to
provide for the Code of Conduct for Ministers of the North‑West Frontier
Province in the manner hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the Provincial
Assembly is not in session and the Governor of the North‑West Frontier
Province is satisfied that the circumstances exist which render it necessary to
take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of
the powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 128 of the Constitution of the
Islamic Republic of Pakistan, the Governor of the North‑West Frontier
Province is pleased to make and promulgate the following Ordinance:‑‑
3. Loyalty.‑‑The
guiding principle for the conduct of Ministers is embodied in the oath of
office that pledges them to bear true faith and allegiance to Pakistan, to
discharge their duties honestly and faithfully in accordance with the law, and
in the interest of ‑the sovereignty, solidarity, well‑being and
prosperity of Pakistan, to strive to preserve the Islamic Ideology which is the
basis for the creation of Pakistan, and not to allow personal interest to
influence their official decisions.

Collective responsibility

following Ordinance by the Governor of the North‑West Frontier Province
is hereby published for general information:
Whereas it is expedient to
provide for the Code of Conduct for Ministers of the North‑West Frontier
Province in the manner hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the Provincial
Assembly is not in session and the Governor of the North‑West Frontier
Province is satisfied that the circumstances exist which render it necessary to
take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of
the powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 128 of the Constitution of the
Islamic Republic of Pakistan, the Governor of the North‑West Frontier
Province is pleased to make and promulgate the following Ordinance:‑‑
4. Collective responsibility.‑‑Ministers
are expected to act as a team loyally in carrying out the task of Government,
and in accordance with the principle of collective responsibility. Each
Minister shall, therefore, respect all policy decisions of Government even if
he personally disagrees with any particular decision, and shall refrain from
expressing views contrary to, or inconsistent with, such a decision. He has the
option to resign, but in no case shall he try to absolve himself of the
responsibility for the decision by disassociating himself from if while he
continues to be a Minister.

Performance of functions and personal responsibility

NORTH﷓WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE MIMSTERS (CODE OF CONDUCT)
ORDINANCE, 1997
NORTH‑WEST FRONTIER
PROVINCE MIMSTERS (CODE OF CONDUCT) ORDINANCE, 1997
An Ordinance to provide for the
Code of Conduct for Ministers of the North‑West Frontier Province
[Gazette of N.‑W.F.P.,
Extraordinary 27th January, 1997].
No Legis. 1(3)/97/581, dated 27‑1‑1997.‑‑‑The
following Ordinance by the Governor of the North‑West Frontier Province
is hereby published for general information:
Whereas it is expedient to
provide for the Code of Conduct for Ministers of the North‑West Frontier
Province in the manner hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the Provincial
Assembly is not in session and the Governor of the North‑West Frontier
Province is satisfied that the circumstances exist which render it necessary to
take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of
the powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 128 of the Constitution of the
Islamic Republic of Pakistan, the Governor of the North‑West Frontier
Province is pleased to make and promulgate the following Ordinance:‑‑
5. Performance of functions
and personal responsibility.‑‑In the performance of their
duties and functions the overriding consideration of Ministers shall be guided
by the national interest and not of the interest of a particular region or of a
particular section of the people or persons. In particular, a Minister shall
not pass any order or direction, whether written or oral, on matters pertaining
to appointment, promotion, posting and transfer of civil servants, or regarding
selection of site, allocation and disbursement of funds, acquisition of land,
or sale, leasing and renting of Government land/structure, or other individual
cases pertaining to day to day administration and conduct of business of a
Department, an Attached Department and other statutory and non‑statutory
bodies under its administrative control.
(2) Without prejudice to the
generality of the provisions contained in sub section (1), it shall be the
responsibility of the Minister to ensure that in respect of the Department or
Departments under his charge the practices of‑‑
(a) submission of Schedule of New
Expenditures and Planning Commission‑IV forms for non‑existent
schemes and institutions;
(b) recruitment against
anticipated vacancies recruitment, posting, transfer and promotions in
violation of law/rules;
(c) selection of sites for
projects and schemes in violation of prescribed criteria;
(d) diversion of funds from an
approved to an unapproved scheme in violation of any rules for the time being
in force;
(e) expenditure on revenue side
without following the financial rules and codal formalities;
(f) non‑observance of
approved planning criteria and procedure governing approval and execution;
(g) non‑observance/contravention
or relaxation of the provisions of the G.F.R. works codes and Audits Treasury
Rules, regarding transfer, sale lease and auction of State land other
properties, and allotment of plots under schemes managed or controlled by or
under the supervision of Government;
(h) improper use or utilization
of maintenance and repair funds, including preparation of fake muster rolls;
(i) purchase of land for
developmental schemes without following the land acquisition procedures;
(j) opening of educational or
technical institutions at places not suitable for such institutions; and
(k) any other practice or
procedure in violation or contravention of any law or rules for the time being
in force,
are strictly done away with.
Explanation. For the
purposes of this subsection, it shall be the duty of the Secretary concerned to
submit all cases falling within the purview thereof to the Minister for his
specific orders.
(3) Contravention of any of the
provisions of subsection (1) or subsection (2) shall be misconduct on the part
of the Minister or the Secretary concerned, as the case may be, and will expose
them to action as warranted by any law for the time being in

Statements and utterances

provide for the Code of Conduct for Ministers of the North‑West Frontier
Province in the manner hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the Provincial

Now, therefore, in exercise of
the powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 128 of the Constitution of the
Islamic Republic of Pakistan, the Governor of the North‑West Frontier
Province is pleased to make and promulgate the following Ordinance:‑‑
6. Statements and utterances.‑‑(1)
Unless it is necessary to do so in defence of a Government decision, a Minister
shall confine his public statement to matters relating to the portfolio under
his own charge. Particular care must be taken in respect of statements bearing
on foreign affairs or relation with other States.
(2) Care must also be taken by a
Minister when making a public statement relating to a proposal, scheme, or a
policy that might be under Government consideration, and on which a final
decision is in doubt Special care is required in respect of statement regarding
duties or taxes, and nothing shall be said to give the slightest cause for
speculation regarding these.

7. Privately arranged
ceremonials, occasions and other private functions.‑‑Before
accepting invitation from private persons or non‑official bodies to
inaugurate, preside over, or be chief guest at public functions, a Minister
shall check up their antecedents with the local authorities or the concerned
Department.

8. Social functions held by
Diplomatic Corps.‑‑Unless it is necessary for official reasons,
a Minister shall not accept invitation to social functions held by the members
of the Diplomatic Corps. As regards official receptions by the foreign
Missions, it will be for the Chief Minister to request one or more Ministers to
attend.

9. Meeting with dignitary from
a foreign country or members of the Diplomatic Corps.‑‑When a
dignitary from a foreign country or a member of the Diplomatic Corps desires to
meet a Minister on official business, the Minister shall ensure that the
discussion is confined to question with which the Department under his control
is competent to deal with. If questions of foreign policy or political
relations are raised, directly or by implication, the dignitary or member of
the Diplomatic Corps shall be advised to take up such question with the
Ministry of Foreign Affairs. A copy of the record of the discussion with the
dignitary of member of the Diplomatic Corps shall be furnished to the
Department concerned. If possible a representative of the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs of appropriate status, should be present during such a meeting.

Whereas it is expedient to

11. Non‑acceptance of
gifts, etc.‑‑A Minister shall not receive any gifts from his
subordinates. If a visiting foreign dignitary presents a gift to a Minister,
which becomes embarrassing to decline, it shall be reported to the Secretary to
Chief Minister indicating whether the Minister would wish to retain it. The
value of the gift will be assessed, and if it exceeds Rs.1,000 the Minister
will be required to pay the difference worked out in accordance with the
instructions in force. If he does not wish to retain it, the gift will be deposited
in the Toshakhana. This rule will also apply to the wife and dependants of the
Minister.

12. Declaration of assets.‑‑Every
Minister on assuming and relinquishing office will fill in the pro forma
according to the format laid down in the Appendix for declaration of his assets
and the assets of his wife and dependants.
This will be sent in duplicate in
a sealed confidential cover to the Secretary to Chief Minister. Changes, if
any, will be intimated on or immediately after occurrence.

13. Private transactions of a
pecuniary or a business nature.‑‑A Minister shall not associate
himself with any public or private company or enter into partnership, during
his tenure of office, except in the following capacities;‑‑
(a) Shareholder,
(b) Sleeping partner,
(e) Honorary Director of a non‑profit
making institution, and
(d) ex‑officio Director on
behalf of Government in a company in which Government has invested from public
funds.

had to disassociate himself under section 13. This also applies to the sole
proprietorship firms.

15. Speculation in investment.‑‑A
Minister shall not speculate in investment and for this purpose habitual
purchase and sale of securities of notoriously fluctuating value will be deemed
to be speculation in investments. He shall also not make or permit any member
of his family to make any investment likely to embarrass or influence him in
the discharge of his official Nor shall he make any investment the value of
which is likely to be by some event of which information is available to him as
a Minister, and is not equally available to the general public.

16. Tour abroad.---For

time, shall be strictly observed by the Minister. Notice of the tours, with its
details, shall be given to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in good time, so
that it may make proper arrangements with, or through, the Government of
countries concerned. The Minister shall politely decline any offer by a private
institution to pay for his expenses during his visit abroad.

sections.description:
Tour abroad

ORDINANCE, 1997
NORTH‑WEST FRONTIER
PROVINCE MIMSTERS (CODE OF CONDUCT) ORDINANCE, 1997
An Ordinance to provide for the
Code of Conduct for Ministers of the North‑West Frontier Province
[Gazette of N.‑W.F.P.,
Extraordinary 27th January, 1997].
No Legis. 1(3)/97/581, dated 27‑1‑1997.‑‑‑The
following Ordinance by the Governor of the North‑West Frontier Province
is hereby published for general information:
Whereas it is expedient to
provide for the Code of Conduct for Ministers of the North‑West Frontier
Province in the manner hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the Provincial
Assembly is not in session and the Governor of the North‑West Frontier
Province is satisfied that the circumstances exist which render it necessary to
take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of
the powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 128 of the Constitution of the
Islamic Republic of Pakistan, the Governor of the North‑West Frontier
Province is pleased to make and promulgate the following Ordinance:‑‑
17.‑‑(1) A
Minister may undertake a tour of the Province as and when he considers it
necessary to be in the public interest. However, if practicable, he may inform
the Chief Minister well in time of his intention to undertake the tour so that
the Chief Minister is aware of his proposed tour and may entrust him with
duties to perform on the tour.
(2) As required under the Rules
of Business, a Minister shall so arrange his tour programme that he is able to
attend the Cabinet meeting, unless he has obtained the permission to absent
himself from the meeting.
(3) A Minister shall so arrange
his tour that he is at the headquarters at least one week before the
commencement of a session of the Provincial Assembly.

18. In respect of
administrative matters relating to the Department under their charge, not
expressly provided for in the Ordinance, Ministers may issue general
directions, or standing instructions, whenever necessary. They shall not
concern themselves with individual cases, unless a breach of rules, general

following Ordinance by the Governor of the North‑West Frontier Province
is hereby published for general information:
Whereas it is expedient to
provide for the Code of Conduct for Ministers of the North‑West Frontier
Province in the manner hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the Provincial
Assembly is not in session and the Governor of the North‑West Frontier

Now, therefore, in exercise of
the powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 128 of the Constitution of the
Islamic Republic of Pakistan, the Governor of the North‑West Frontier

19. Minister should set an
example of simplicity and austerity by their public conduct, and by shunning
ostentatious living and lavish entertainment. It is expected that all Ministers
will set personal example in the performance of "Deeni Faraiz", in
the use of Pakistani dress and national language.
